R2B-bear-drive-0003.name: 280 m N of Elaho River
R2B-bear-drive-0003.pressureWhy: No town, pavement or rec site within 1 km and not behind a closure (estimate).

evidence.t: Cutblock harvested 2015 (11 years old), 20 m SE: cutblocks and logging road edges green up first in spring (65%) and grow berries for the fall feed (lesson: Black bear).
Burn from 2015 (fire V30160), right here: burned areas are spring bear food (90%) and huckleberry grows in old burns (80%) (lessons: Black bear Masterclass 5, Habitat tour).
W facing slope, 26 degrees: grassy south facing slopes are spring bear food (90%, lesson: Black bear Masterclass 5).
Unnamed wetland right here: stream sides and skunk cabbage swamps are spring food, and bears forage on berries and spawning fish in fall (90%, lesson: Black bear Masterclass 5).
1 km or more from pavement and 2 km from a town: bears near people feed more at night (75%, lesson: Black bear Masterclass 6).

plan: Drive: from District of Squamish, about 77 km (straight line times 1.3, estimate).
Park: 50.24527, -123.56711, pull off on Blk 71-63 (gravel road). Map links below.
Walk: none. The spot is at the road.

Hunt: black bear, Apr, May, June, Sept, Oct, Nov (season rows). Glass berry slopes, cutblocks and road edges at dawn and the last 2 hours of light, wind in your face (Tip). A bear under 2 years old and any bear with it are closed (99%, synopsis page 11).
Use: your .308 Winchester with a 150 to 180 grain expanding bullet (Tip).
Legal: MU (Management Unit) 2-6, Region 2. Season rows below. Study aid only. The official regulations are the law.
Verify: Candidate, scout it first. Check posted signs. Private land can be unsigned. Data dates: roads 2026-10-16, private land 2026-10-09, closures 2026-10-16.
R2B-bear-drive-0003.popWhy: Less popular (quieter): MU 2-6: about 312 hunter days a year for black bear (2020 to 2024 mean), 0.11 days per square km, middle third of BC MUs; access: average access. Estimate, about 50% sure (my pick).

tags.label: Good solo
tags.why: Short pack out: 0.0 km and about 0 m of climb from the parking (Tip). Cell coverage is not in the data: leave a trip plan and carry SOS or a satellite messenger (lesson: Bush safety).

R2B-deer-backcountry-0004.name: 250 m E of Stakawus Creek
R2B-deer-backcountry-0004.pressureWhy: More than 5 km from a drivable road (estimate).
R2B-deer-backcountry-0004.parkWhat: pull off on an unnamed paved road

evidence.t: Deer here are black tailed deer, the coast form of mule deer: the synopsis calls them "mule (black-tailed) deer" (99%, Rule Book: Region 2 Lower Mainland).
Mule deer winter range u-2-011 unit JR 06 (official), 340 m E. Counts from October.
Cutblock harvested 2013 (13 years old), right here.
Habitat zone Coastal Western Hemlock (CWHvm1): coast forest, where black tailed deer are among the most common large mammals (95%) and use logged ground often (80%) (lesson: Wet forests).
SW facing slope, 15 degrees: sun melts snow first.
Black bear: young cutblocks and burns grow berries in late summer and fall (Tip).

plan: Drive: from District of Squamish, about 70 km (straight line times 1.3, estimate).
Park: 49.91715, -123.86556, pull off on an unnamed paved road. Map links below.
Walk: 17 km NE, cross country, no trail mapped. Climb about 2,257 m, about 571 min at 3 km/h.
Camp: flat ground 150 m SW of the spot at 230 m (50.04181, -123.72612). Water: Stakawus Creek 130 m SW (estimate).
Hunt: deer, Sept, Oct, Nov (season rows). Watch the edge of the 2013 cutblock (right here) at first and last light. Sit above it with the wind in your face and glass (Tip).
Use: your .308 Winchester with a 150 to 165 grain expanding bullet (Tip).
Legal: MU (Management Unit) 2-5, Region 2. Season rows below. Study aid only. The official regulations are the law.
Verify: Candidate, scout it first. Check posted signs. Private land can be unsigned. Data dates: roads 2026-10-16, private land 2026-10-09, closures 2026-10-16.
